title: Unused BigQuery key-file credentials must not block source setup
answers: Why does BigQuery setup list missing JSON fields when I selected a service account?
Can an empty key file from the unselected auth option block saving?
How should BigQuery replace generic required-field errors?
body:
Symptom: Connecting BigQuery with a selected Google Cloud service account fails with missing JSON key-field errors despite a complete selection.
Root cause: products/warehouse_sources/backend/temporal/data_imports/sources/common/config.py:validate_config validates nested key-file fields; the wizard can send an empty key file for the unselected option.
Fix pattern: products/warehouse_sources/backend/temporal/data_imports/sources/bigquery/source.py:BigQuerySource.validate_config removes errors identified by _KEY_FILE_FIELD_ERRORS, recomputes validity from remaining errors, and then checks the selected credential. Construct matching errors through products/warehouse_sources/backend/temporal/data_imports/sources/common/config.py:missing_field_error so producer and filter share wording.
Constraints: Suppress only the key-file required-field errors, preserving other validation failures and the selected-credential check. Keep this behavior in the BigQuery override; it does not establish a shared-walker policy for other sources.
applies: BigQuery source configuration validation when payloads include credentials for both authentication options.
